202611171427-n2-never-name-a-number-firs.topic: 'Never name a number first' is only half right: the salary-expectations script for the recruiter's first call

script.title: "Never Name a Number First" Is Only Half Right

beats.narration: "Never name a number first" is only half right.
"I'm flexible" sounds unprepared, and the recruiter still has a number in mind. It's theirs.
Try: "Based on what I'm seeing for this role, I'm targeting eighty to ninety thousand. How does that fit your range?"
Make the bottom of that range a number you'd genuinely accept. That's the one they'll hear.
If the role is vague, the old rule holds. Ask: "What's the budgeted range?" Some US states require posted ranges, so check the listing first.
You have less leverage here. A researched range still beats a shrug.
Save this script for the next time you need it, and tell me in the comments which piece of career advice I should test next.

script.title: Edinburgh in 48 Hours of Rain: Two Free Museums and a Pub Lunch

beats.narration: Two days of Edinburgh rain? Plan around two free buildings.

Constraint: constant rain, modest budget. Day one is the National Museum of Scotland. Free entry to the permanent galleries, opens about ten. Check for any charged special exhibitions. The cost: wet-morning crowds, so arrive early.
Lunch is a pub nearby. Mains often run around fifteen pounds or more, so check menus, and accept steamed-up windows.
Day two: the Scottish National Gallery on the Mound. Free permanent collection, a short walk away. Restless kids? Repeat the museum instead.
Skip the Castle in heavy rain. It has lots of outdoor walkways, and cloud eats the views you're paying for. Some indoor areas stay open.
Tell me your city and your constraint in the comments, and I'll build the plan in a future video.

202611171434-n2-what-happens-if-you-coun.topic: What happens if you counter the first offer by asking for a bit more

script.title: What Happens If You Counter the First Job Offer?

beats.narration: What actually happens when you counter the first offer? A polite ask is meant to start a conversation, not end one.
Say this: "I'm excited about the role. Based on the scope, I was hoping for closer to seventy-two thousand. Is there any flexibility?"
Weaker version: "Is that the best you can do?" That's haggling.

If pay bands are fixed or there's a hiring freeze, ask about a signing bonus, extra leave, or an earlier review. Offers can sometimes be withdrawn before you accept, depending on local law. This isn't legal advice.
